o: One operation rotates s left by taking a suffix of length l (1 ≤ l ≤ n−1) and moving it to the front — i.e., a cyclic shift by any nonzero amount. Count sequences of exactly k operations turning s into t. All reachable strings are rotations of s; let m = number of nonzero shifts l with rot(s, l) = t. By symmetry, from any state u the number of shifts landing on a fixed target-state set behaves uniformly: from a state equal to t, m shifts stay in {t}; from any other state, n−1−m shifts land in {t}. With a₀ = [s==t], the counts evolve by the 2×2 matrix [[m, n−1−m],[n−1−m, m−1]] raised to the k-th power. Example 1 (abcd→cdab, k=2): m=1 gives answer 2; Example 2 (ababab, k=1): m=2 gives 2.
k: Operations are cyclic shifts; whether rot(u,l)=t depends only on l, so transitions are uniform across states.
m = #{l ∈ [1,n−1] : rot(s,l)=t} = occurrences of t in s+s at start positions 1..n−1 (find via KMP).
Answer = first component of M^k·(a₀,b₀) with M = [[m, n−1−m],[n−1−m, m−1]]; use fast matrix exponentiation since k ≤ 10¹⁵.

a.i: Maintain (a, b) = (#ways currently at a string equal to t, at any other string). Each step: a' = m·a + (n−1−m)·b, b' = (n−1−m)·a + (m−1)·b. Clear and correct but O(k) — only feasible for small k; motivates the matrix version.
s: Compute m by shifting and comparing (naive) or KMP.
Iterate the recurrence k times modulo 1e9+7.
a.t: O(n² ) to compute m naively plus O(k) iterations — fine only for small k; included for intuition.

a.i: Compute m in O(n) with KMP by counting matches of t inside s+s restricted to start positions 1..n−1. Then raise the 2×2 transition matrix to the k-th power in O(log k). Handles k up to 10¹⁵ easily.
s: KMP-search t in s+s; count matches starting at positions 1..n−1 → m.
Build M = [[m, n−1−m],[n−1−m, m−1]] mod p.
a.t: O(n) for KMP matching plus O(log k) 2×2 matrix multiplications.
a.sp: O(n) for the text and failure table.

w: Always present the matrix-power solution in interviews — k up to 10¹⁵ rules out iteration. Pitfalls: including shift l=0 or l=n when counting m (both forbidden), forgetting periodic strings like "ababab" where m>1, and negative (m−1) before the modulus in C++/Java. Follow-up: count transformations in at most k operations, or restrict allowed shift lengths to a set.
